basic_identification.full_title: Hot Rolled Steel Narrow Width Strip for Welded Tubes and Pipes — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering (finalised by the Wrought Steel Products Sectional Committee and approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard covers the requirements for weldable quality hot rolled narrow width steel strips up to 600 mm in width for the manufacture of steel pipes and tubes intended for non-critical applications (such as low pressure water and furniture purposes). It explicitly excludes and states that these strips are not applicable for manufacturing steel pipes for pressure applications such as high pressure water, steam, oil, and gases.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: According to the product standard text, certification is permissive: conforming material 'may also be marked' with the BIS Standard Mark under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986. While the certification is voluntary in the text, the code establishes clear manufacturer markings, strict batch chemical ladle analysis, physical test sampling schedules, and retesting compliance rules.

requirements.detail: The hot rolled narrow width steel strip conforming to this standard may also be marked with the Standard Mark under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (now 2016), and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder.
Every narrow width strip or bundle must be legibly marked on either the inside or outside with the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, grade of steel (Grade 1, 2, or 3), cast or lot number, and size.
Material supply must be ordered and verified on the basis of either its chemical composition or physical properties as agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser.

Ladle analysis must be carried out on each heat/20 tonnes (or part thereof) to verify compliance with specified maximum chemical constituent limits for Carbon, Manganese, Sulphur, Phosphorus, Silicon, Aluminum, and Nitrogen.

One physical sample must be tested for each heat/20 tonnes per thickness per cast. Tensile samples must be taken longitudinally and meet mechanical minimums in Table 3. Bend tests must be taken transversally and bent cold through 180 degrees without showing cracks on the outer convex surface.

If any primary test piece fails to pass any physical test, two further samples from the same lot must be tested for that failure. The lot is accepted only if both additional test pieces pass; if either fails, the lot is deemed non-conforming and rejected.

The steel must be free from defects like segregation, lamination, and surface flaws that would harm subsequent processing. When mill edges are specified, the depth of edge defects must fall within 5 mm from either side.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15647:2006 is the national Indian Standard specification for weldable quality hot-rolled narrow width steel strips (commonly referred to in India as 'Patra') up to 600 mm in width. It applies specifically to strips used to manufacture welded tubes and pipes intended for non-critical, structural, or low-pressure domestic applications (such as low-pressure water and furniture). It explicitly prohibits use in high-pressure pressure pipes (e.g. steam, high-pressure water, oil, and gas lines). When sourcing these steel strips, engineers must verify that chemical parameters (such as the Carbon, Manganese, Sulphur, and Phosphorus limits for Grades 1, 2, and 3) are satisfied via ladle checks, and ensure that physical strength (tensile, yield, and cold-bend ductility) is verified per cast and thickness.
